verdicts.reason: Both drop the original idea of the quote sitting inside the illustrated frame and instead show the frame artwork, with its stock 'BEAUTY ILLUSTRATION / HAND DRAWN ELEMENTS' text, as a small thumbnail. In both, the quote wraps one or two words per line and runs almost to the side edges. A keeps the quote and 'CAROLYN MURPHY' together in a sensible order (art, then quote, then author), but the attribution is jammed right under 'MAKEUP.' and close to the bottom edge. B puts the artwork between the quote and its attribution, so the author name is cut off from its quote and reads like a caption for the picture. That broken grouping makes B the weaker of the two.
